issues.legal_issue: An official entrusted with delegated statutory discretion must exercise independent judgment and cannot implement a superior official’s binding direction without authority to do so.
material_facts: The Cane Commissioner had concluded that the existing reservation should not be disturbed and had recommended against changing it.
The Chief Minister directed that the reserved villages be divided between the two mills and specified how they should be allocated.
The Cane Commissioner issued the challenged orders carrying out that direction.
issues.conclusion: The challenged orders were invalid because the Chief Minister, rather than the Cane Commissioner, exercised the statutory power, and the Commissioner did not exercise his own judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Under clauses 6 and 11 of the Sugar Cane (Control) Order, 1955, the power was exercisable by the delegated authority, which could not abdicate its responsibility to a superior unless binding instructions were expressly authorized. An official may consider relevant government policy but must exercise personal judgment in an individual case. The Court applied Commissioner of Police, Bombay v. Gordhandas Bhanji, [1952] S.C.R. 135, and State of Punjab v. Hari Kishan Sharma, A.I.R. 1966 S.C. 1081.

rule.if: challenge_to_modified_sugarcane_reservation and superior_directed_the_outcome and delegated_official_opposed_the_change and delegated_official_followed_the_direction and not binding_superior_instruction_authorized

predicates.challenge_to_modified_sugarcane_reservat: A party challenged an order changing an existing sugarcane reservation.
predicates.superior_directed_the_outcome: A superior official directed how the disputed reservation should be changed.
predicates.delegated_official_opposed_the_change: The official entrusted with the decision had expressed the view that the existing reservation should not be changed.
predicates.delegated_official_followed_the_directio: The entrusted official issued an order implementing the superior official’s direction.
predicates.binding_superior_instruction_authorized: A governing legal rule authorized the superior official to give binding instructions on the decision.

issues.definition: When a challenged reservation change was directed by a superior, opposed by the entrusted official, and implemented by that official without authority for binding instructions, the order is invalid as not having been made by the prescribed authority.

issues.legal_issue: A contested decision altering an existing sugarcane reservation that adversely affects a factory’s interests is quasi-judicial, and the affected factory must have a fair opportunity to address the case and proposed change.
material_facts: A competing mill sought to have villages taken out of the area already reserved for the appellant mill and allocated to itself.
The dispute had to be determined by reference to the factories’ crushing capacity, the availability of sugarcane, and the need for sugar production.
Changing the reservation would adversely affect the appellant mill’s interests and its supply of sugarcane.
The competing mill’s representations, and the proposal for dividing the villages, were not disclosed to the appellant mill, which had no opportunity to object to the proposed division.
issues.conclusion: The proceeding was quasi-judicial, and the failure to disclose the case and proposed division and provide an opportunity to respond contravened natural justice; the challenged orders could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: Where a statutory authority resolves a dispute between opposing claimants using objective criteria, and its decision prejudicially affects a claimant’s interests, the proceeding is quasi-judicial unless the governing law indicates otherwise. The affected party must receive a fair opportunity to address the material case and proposed decision. The Court relied on clause 6 of the Sugar Cane (Control) Order, 1955, Province of Bombay v. Kusaldas S. Advani, [1950] S.C.R. 621 at 725, Shivji Nathubhai v. Union of India, [1960] 2 S.C.R. 775, Board of High School and Intermediate Education, U.P., Allahabad v. Ghanshyam Das Gupta, [1962] 3 Supp. S.C.R. 36, New Zealand Dairy Board v. Okitu Co-operative Dairy Co. Ltd., (1953) N.Z.L.R. 366, James Edward Jeffs v. New Zealand Dairy Production and Marketing Board, [1967] A.C. 551, and Suresh Koshy George v. University of Kerala, [1969] 1 S.C.R. 317.

rule.if: challenge_to_modified_sugarcane_reservation and competing_claimants_disputed_the_allocation and objective_criteria_governed_the_decision and change_adversely_affected_existing_beneficiary and relevant_case_or_proposed_change_was_not_disclosed and affected_party_had_no_opportunity_to_respond

predicates.challenge_to_modified_sugarcane_reservat: A party challenged a decision altering an existing sugarcane reservation.
predicates.competing_claimants_disputed_the_allocat: Two competing factories advanced opposing claims to the reserved area.
predicates.objective_criteria_governed_the_decision: The dispute was to be resolved by considering relevant operational and supply factors.
predicates.change_adversely_affected_existing_benef: The proposed change would adversely affect the interests of the factory already benefiting from the reservation.
predicates.relevant_case_or_proposed_change_was_not: The opposing claimant’s representations or the proposed manner of changing the allocation were not made known to the affected factory.
predicates.affected_party_had_no_opportunity_to_res: The affected factory was not given an opportunity to object to the undisclosed case or proposed change.

issues.definition: When competing claimants dispute an allocation governed by objective criteria, the change adversely affects an existing beneficiary, and that beneficiary cannot respond to the undisclosed case or proposed change, the order is invalid for denial of a fair hearing.

issues.legal_issue: A factory whose existing reserved area is reduced is an aggrieved party even if no further orders governing supply or purchase have been made.
material_facts: The challenged order removed villages from the area reserved for the appellant mill and added them to the area reserved for a competing mill.
The change prevented the appellant mill from obtaining sugarcane from the affected villages.
No orders had yet been made under the provisions governing growers’ supply obligations or factories’ purchase obligations.
issues.conclusion: The appellant mill was an aggrieved party because the challenged change itself adversely affected its interests; further supply or purchase orders were not necessary.
issues.legal_principle: A party is aggrieved when the challenged order directly and adversely affects its interests. The absence of later orders governing supply or purchase does not remove that direct effect where the challenged order takes away part of the party’s reserved source of sugarcane.

predicates.challenge_to_modified_sugarcane_reservat: A party challenged a decision altering an existing sugarcane reservation.
predicates.existing_beneficiary_lost_part_of_reserv: The order removed part of the area previously reserved for the factory.
predicates.loss_adversely_affected_its_interests: The removed area could no longer serve as a source of sugarcane for that factory.

issues.definition: When an order changing a reservation takes away part of an existing beneficiary’s sugarcane source and thereby adversely affects its interests, that beneficiary is an aggrieved party.

issues.legal_issue: A state authority empowered to reserve sugarcane-growing areas within its jurisdiction may reserve such an area for a factory located outside that state.
material_facts: The appellant’s mill was located in one state, while the villages at issue were in a neighboring state.
The Cane Commissioner had authority over reservations of sugarcane-growing areas within the state where the villages were located.
issues.conclusion: The Cane Commissioner could reserve the area for a sugar mill whether that mill was located inside or outside the state.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 6 of the Sugar Cane (Control) Order, 1955, read with clause 11 and the delegation of powers, empowered the Cane Commissioner to reserve an area within the Commissioner’s jurisdiction for a sugar factory; the factory’s location outside that state did not disqualify it.

predicates.sugarcane_reservation_proceeding: An authority considered reserving a sugarcane-growing area for a factory.
predicates.area_within_authority_jurisdiction: The sugarcane-growing area was within the territorial jurisdiction of the authority making the reservation.
predicates.factory_located_outside_that_jurisdictio: The factory for which the area was considered was located outside the authority’s territorial jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When an authority considers a reservation for a factory located elsewhere, it may reserve an area within its jurisdiction for that factory.
